newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INDUSTRIAL INVESTMENT TO FALL 1997-98 - TT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INDUSTRIAL INVESTMENT TO FALL 1997-98 - TT.

text.p: The industry's fixed investments
are expected to fall 7.7 percent in 1997 and by a further 13.8
percent in 1998, the Confederation of Finnish Industry and
Employers's (TT) said in its semi-annual survey on Monday.
Last year, industrial investment was boosted to a 17 percent
increase by large forest industry investments which have now
been completed, it said.
TT's semi-annual survey of some 420 industrial companies
accounting for 90 percent of all domestic manufacturing industry
investments showed investment growth in 1997 in the base metals,
engineering and chemical industries.
Fixed investment Yr/Yr change
(billion markka) (pct)
Forest industry 10.6 7.9 6.8 -25.7 -14.3*
--electrotechnical 1.9 1.9 1.5 -1.2 -17.6*
Chemical industry 1.7 2.3 2.8 +32.9 -18.8*
MANUFACTURING
*TT said respondents in previous surveys had tended to
understate the following year's investments.
Manufacturing industry investments in machinery and
equipment this year would shrink by about one percent with
growth in machinery and equipment investment in most key
industries expected to offset a forecast 21 percent fall in such
forest industry investment, TT said.
The value of total machinery and equipment investment would
be about 15.2 billion markka in 1997, it said.
The manufacturing industry's R&D spending would rise 19
percent this year to 8.6 billion markka, but fall slightly in
1998, it said.
